spec.objective: Write the hermetic wired oracle tests/test_cloner_wired.py that exercises the real clone path of ngv2.acquisition.cloner against a local bare-repo fixture over file://, asserting every brief-mandated behavior.
functional_requirements: Construct a LOCAL bare git repository fixture (via git init/commit into a bare repo or temp dir) and drive clone_target with a real-git runner (make_subprocess_runner) over a file:// URL so the test is hermetic.
Assert the returned Target.pinned_commit equals the fixture's HEAD SHA and Target.validate() passed (non-empty fields, loc>=0).

Assert clone_target writes the clone under an in-tree dest_root (tmp/ supplied as a pytest tmp_path-rooted in-tree dir) and never under /tmp, and that primary language + LOC are detected from the fixture source files.
Assert archived=True raises CloneError before any runner invocation (inject a runner that records calls and assert it was not called).
Assert a size_cap breach (size_cap_mb=0 or tiny) raises CloneError after a successful clone.
Assert reuse=True reuses a populated clone dir instead of re-cloning (inject a counting runner and assert clone was invoked only once across two calls).
Assert a non-zero rc from the injected runner for `git clone` and for `git rev-parse HEAD` each raise CloneError.
spec.interfaces: Imports clone_target, make_subprocess_runner, CloneError from ngv2.acquisition.cloner and ngv2.contracts.Target; uses pytest tmp_path and a local bare-repo fixture; injects deterministic now() for cloned_at.
edge_cases: Empty-but-existing clone dir with reuse=True must trigger a real re-clone.
file:// URL with and without a trailing .git suffix both resolve to a stable slug.
Counting runner must distinguish `git clone` calls from `git rev-parse` calls.
non_goals: No network access, no real remote hosting.
Do not modify ngv2.acquisition.cloner, ngv2.contracts, or harness/target_bootstrap.py.
No auto-submit, scan, detonate, LLM, or randomness.
spec.implementation_notes: Use a deterministic injected now() to make cloned_at stable. Use a real-git runner for the happy path so the genuine clone/rev-parse path is exercised, and lightweight fake runners (recording/counting/forced-rc) for the archived, cache-reuse, and error-path assertions. Ensure dest_root is an in-tree directory under the repo (e.g. a tmp/ subdir created from the test) rather than /tmp.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: A local bare git repository fixture created at test time containing source files of known extensions (e.g. .py) with known line counts; accessed only over file://.

token_budget_ratio.note: Pure test-authoring task; all budget goes to the committed oracle that must pass on the verbatim module and fail on its declared mutant.

tasks.title: Create ngv2/acquisition/cloner.py io_adapter: shallow clone into in-tree tmp/ returning typed Target
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/acquisition/cloner.py exists with EXACTLY the content given in the brief Deliverables (verbatim).
Module is importable as ngv2.acquisition.cloner (namespace package, no new __init__.py).
clone_target(repo_url, *, dest_root='tmp', runner=None, now=None, size_cap_mb=500, archived=False, reuse=True) returns a validated ngv2.contracts.Target.
make_subprocess_runner() returns the production subprocess-backed Runner seam; CloneError is exported.
No other module is touched; ngv2.contracts and harness/target_bootstrap.py are unchanged.

spec.objective: Emit a new io_adapter module ngv2/acquisition/cloner.py verbatim from the brief that shallow-clones a target repository into an in-tree tmp/ directory and returns a typed ngv2.contracts.Target, with all impure git/filesystem operations behind injected seams.
functional_requirements: clone_target performs `git clone --depth 1 <repo_url> <repo_root>` into the in-tree dest_root (default 'tmp'), creating dest_root if needed; it NEVER clones into /tmp.
After clone, the pinned HEAD commit SHA is recorded by invoking `git rev-parse HEAD` (cwd=repo_root) and stored on Target.pinned_commit.
A size cap is enforced by summing on-disk file bytes under repo_root; if it exceeds size_cap_mb*1024*1024 a CloneError is raised.
Primary language is detected by source-file count using the _LANG_BY_EXT mapping, returning 'unknown' when no source files are found (.git tree skipped).
LOC is counted as newline-terminated lines across detected source files (.git tree skipped).
Archived repos are refused up front: archived=True raises CloneError before any runner call.
Clone cache/reuse: with reuse=True an existing populated repo_root is reused instead of re-cloning; otherwise an existing dir is removed and a fresh clone is run.

All git invocations go through the injected `runner(argv, cwd) -> (rc, stdout, stderr)` seam (default make_subprocess_runner()) and the clock goes through the injected `now() -> str` seam (default _default_now); make_subprocess_runner() returns the production subprocess seam.
The returned Target is constructed with repo_url, resolved repo_root, pinned_commit, language, loc, cloned_at and target.validate() is called before return.
spec.interfaces: exposes `clone_target(repo_url, *, dest_root='tmp', runner=None, now=None, size_cap_mb=500, archived=False, reuse=True) -> ngv2.contracts.Target`, `make_subprocess_runner() -> Runner`, and `CloneError(RuntimeError)`. Runner = Callable[[Sequence[str], Optional[str]], Tuple[int, str, str]].
edge_cases: git clone returns non-zero rc -> CloneError('git clone failed (rc=...): ...').
git rev-parse returns non-zero rc -> CloneError('git rev-parse failed ...').
repo_root exists but is empty with reuse=True -> treated as not cached, dir removed and re-cloned.
Symlinks and unreadable files during size walk are skipped without error.
repo_url with trailing slash or '.git' suffix still yields a stable filesystem-safe slug.
non_goals: Do NOT clone into /tmp; use in-tree tmp/.
Do NOT call the network or git directly in pure paths; everything git goes through the injected runner seam.
Do NOT modify ngv2.contracts or harness/target_bootstrap.py.
No auto-submit, scan, detonate, LLM, or randomness.
spec.implementation_notes:
Write the file with EXACTLY the content from the brief Deliverables, byte-for-byte (docstring, imports, constants, helpers _slug/_dir_size_bytes/_detect_language/_count_loc/_rmtree/_default_now, and clone_target). Single new file; rely on Python namespace packages so no ngv2/acquisition/__init__.py is added.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: A local bare-repo git fixture with at least one source file of a known extension, cloned over file:// using a real-git runner so the suite is hermetic (no network).
